title: Exoplanet transit in a stellar light curve
text: An exoplanet transit occurs when a planet crosses the stellar disk. The blocked area creates a shallow periodic brightness dip with a depth related to the planet-to-star radius ratio.

title: Diagnostic geometry of a planetary transit
text: Repeated orbital periods, ingress and egress, a flat-bottomed minimum, and nearly constant transit depth distinguish a planet crossing from a one-off lens or a fast stellar flare.

title: Magnetic stellar flare light curve
text: A stellar flare is a magnetic reconnection event that rapidly brightens a star and then decays as heated plasma cools. It may be strong in ultraviolet and X rays.

title: Fast-rise slow-decay flare signature
text: The asymmetric fast rise and slow cooling tail, chromospheric emission, and an X-ray burst separate a magnetic stellar flare from periodic transits and symmetric microlensing.

title: Gravitational microlensing of a background star
text: Microlensing occurs when a foreground mass bends light and temporarily magnifies a more distant background source without resolving multiple images.

title: Achromatic symmetric microlensing event
text: A Paczynski-like curve is approximately symmetric, achromatic, governed by an Einstein timescale, and usually does not repeat. These features contrast with a flare's cooling tail.

title: Pulsar timing residuals
text: A radio pulsar acts as a precise rotating lighthouse. Differences between predicted and observed pulse-arrival times form timing residuals that reveal glitches or companions.

title: Dispersion and cadence in pulsar timing
text: Pulse cadence, spin period, dispersion measure, and a structured timing residual diagnose why regular radio pulses arrive early or late.

title: Fast radio burst transient
text: A fast radio burst is an intense extragalactic radio flash lasting milliseconds. Its signal sweeps across frequency because plasma disperses lower frequencies more strongly.

title: High-dispersion millisecond radio pulse
text: Millisecond duration, a high dispersion measure, and a frequency-dependent sweep identify an FRB; some sources repeat, unlike regular pulsar cadence.

title: Supernova explosion light curve
text: A supernova stellar explosion rapidly brightens and then fades over weeks or months as ejecta expand and deposited energy escapes.

title: Radioactive tail of a supernova
text: A strong explosion peak, expanding spectral ejecta, a multiweek fade, and a nickel-to-cobalt radioactive decay tail distinguish a supernova light curve.

title: Cepheid variable star as a distance indicator
text: A Cepheid is a regularly pulsating variable star. Its pulsation period predicts intrinsic luminosity, so observed brightness yields distance.

title: Cepheid period-luminosity standard candle
text: A stable days-long pulsation, the period-luminosity relation, and its role in the distance ladder identify a Cepheid standard candle.

title: Black-hole accretion disk and corona
text: Gas feeding a black hole forms a hot accretion disk and energetic corona. Changing inflow produces rapid X-ray variability around the compact dark object.

title: X-ray diagnostics of black-hole accretion
text: Disk temperature, an iron emission line, quasi-periodic oscillations, and stochastic X-ray flicker are characteristic diagnostics of a black-hole accretion flow.

title: Compact-binary gravitational-wave chirp
text: Two compact masses in a binary lose orbital energy as gravitational waves. Their inspiral accelerates until merger and produces a characteristic chirp.

title: Rising frequency in an inspiral waveform
text: Increasing frequency and strain amplitude, a measurable chirp mass, and matched-filter consistency discriminate a compact-binary gravitational-wave signal.

title: Spectroscopic galaxy redshift
text: Spectral lines from a receding galaxy appear at longer wavelengths. Comparing observed and laboratory wavelengths gives its cosmological redshift.

title: Red lines and recession velocity
text: A consistent red displacement across known spectral lines, the Hubble relation, and inferred recession velocity distinguish galaxy redshift from an intrinsic color change.

title: Weak lensing map of dark matter
text: Foreground gravity slightly distorts many background galaxy shapes. Their coherent shear statistically maps invisible matter and halo structure.

title: Cosmic shear and convergence
text: Ellipticity correlations, cosmic shear, and a convergence map trace dark-matter halos; the signal is a population-level shape distortion rather than a single magnified star.

title: Cosmic microwave background anisotropy
text: Relic microwave radiation from the early universe contains tiny temperature and polarization variations across the sky.

title: Acoustic peaks in relic radiation
text: Microkelvin temperature fluctuations, acoustic peaks, polarization spectra, and the last-scattering surface are diagnostic of cosmic microwave background anisotropy.

title: Solar coronal mass ejection
text: A coronal mass ejection launches a large magnetized plasma cloud from the Sun into interplanetary space and can create hazardous space weather.

title: Earth-directed CME diagnostics
text: A coronagraph front, Earth-directed trajectory, magnetized cloud, and subsequent geomagnetic storm separate a CME from an electromagnetic solar flare alone.

title: Asteroid occultation of a star
text: An asteroid passing across the line of sight briefly blocks a background star. Observers along its narrow shadow path measure disappearance times.

title: Shadow chords from an occultation
text: A sharp seconds-long light drop, narrow ground track, and multiple shadow chords constrain the small body's outline and identify an asteroid occultation.

title: Stellar tidal disruption by a black hole
text: A star passing within the tidal radius of a massive black hole is torn into debris and powers a luminous flare in a galactic nucleus.

title: Fallback signature of a tidal disruption event
text: A months-long nuclear transient, stellar debris, a characteristic fallback rate, and association with a massive black hole distinguish a tidal disruption event.

title: Neutron-star merger and kilonova
text: Two neutron stars collide and eject neutron-rich matter. The event can emit gravitational waves, a short gamma-ray burst, and a kilonova glow.

title: Heavy-element ejecta from a compact merger
text: R-process heavy elements, red optical emission, fast ejecta, and coincidence with a short gamma-ray burst diagnose a neutron-star merger kilonova.

title: Quasar and active-galactic-nucleus variability
text: A luminous active galactic nucleus changes brightness as the accretion flow around its central massive black hole evolves.

title: Long-timescale stochastic AGN flicker
text: Months-to-years stochastic variability, broad emission lines, and a damped-random-walk signature distinguish quasar variability from short stellar transients.

title: Cloudy brown-dwarf atmosphere
text: A brown dwarf is a cool substellar object whose infrared spectrum probes molecular absorption and patchy atmospheric clouds.

title: Methane and rotational weather on a brown dwarf
text: Methane absorption, unusual infrared colors, and rotational brightness modulation from patchy clouds diagnose a brown-dwarf atmosphere.

title: Protoplanetary disk around a young star
text: Gas and dust orbit a young star in a protoplanetary disk. Rings, gaps, and spirals reveal structure in a forming planetary system.

title: Millimeter rings and gaps in a planet nursery
text: Millimeter continuum emission, a disk gap, a snow line, and spiral structure distinguish a protoplanetary disk and can indicate planet formation.

title: Baryon acoustic oscillation standard ruler
text: Baryon acoustic oscillations leave a preferred large-scale separation in the spatial clustering of galaxies, usable as a cosmological ruler.

title: Sound horizon peak in galaxy clustering
text: A peak in the galaxy correlation function at a preferred separation reflects the sound horizon and constrains cosmic expansion.
